title: Resource tagging and request attribution playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary

This playbook defines the company-wide standards for resource tagging and request attribution. It covers the canonical tag keys for infrastructure and metadata, the HTTP headers and tracing attributes required for request-level attribution, enforcement and validation mechanisms, cost allocation mapping to billing, and rollout/operational steps for teams adopting the standard. The goal is to make resource ownership, cost responsibility, SLO mapping, and root-cause analysis consistent across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Principles

- Single source of truth: Adopt a minimal, well-documented set of tag keys and headers that every service must populate.
- Explicit ownership: Tags must identify owning team, product, and cost center so billing and escalation are unambiguous.
- Low friction: Defaults and automation must minimize developer overhead.
- Observability-first: Tags and headers must support correlation across logs, traces, metrics, and billing.
- Privacy and security: Do not place PII or secrets in tags or headers. Mark sensitive signals as restricted if needed.

Scope

This playbook applies to all services and deployment modes in the Redwood inference stack, including:
- Control plane APIs (hosted control plane)
- Serving runtime and inference gateways
- Sidecars and runtime agents deployed with Private and Dedicated offerings
- Batch jobs and offline pipelines that consume capacity

Canonical Tagging Schema (infrastructure and resources)

Teams must attach the following tags to compute resources (VMs, containers, GPUs), storage buckets, and persistent volumes. These keys are normalized and indexed in the cost accounting pipeline.

| Key | Required | Format / Example | Purpose |
|------|----------|------------------|---------|
| rw.owner | yes | team-slug e.g., team-model-serving | Primary owning team for operational contact and escalations |
| rw.product | yes | product-slug e.g., embeddings-api | Product or product area consuming the resource |
| rw.env | yes | one of {prod, staging, dev, test} | Environment classification for SLO/billing separation |
| rw.cost_center | yes | numeric string or short code e.g., CC-420 | Accounting cost center linked to finance ledger |
| rw.tenant_id | conditional | customer-id or internal for platform | For customer-specific Dedicated/Private resources; blank for control-plane shared infra |
| rw.slo_class | optional | gold | silver | bronze | Used to map resources to latency/availability SLO tiers |
| rw.purpose | optional | inference-cache | training | backup | Free-form short identifier used for quota and lifecycle rules |
| rw.lifecycle | optional | owned | leased | ephemeral | Inform automated garbage collection and reclamation |

Tagging conventions:
- Keys are lowercase, dot-separated prefix 'rw.' to avoid collisions.
- Values should avoid spaces and sensitive data. Use canonical slugs where available.
- rw.tenant_id is mandatory for any customer-dedicated cluster. For hosted multi-tenant nodes, tenant should be left empty and requests carry request-level attribution headers.

Request Attribution (headers and trace attributes)

Every inbound request that can incur cost or affect SLOs must include request-level attribution metadata. This is required for routing, quota checks, cost allocation, and post-incident analysis. The following headers are the canonical set; services must accept them and propagate to downstream services, logs, and traces.

Required HTTP headers:

1. x-rw-request-id: UUIDv4 – Unique request id for deterministic correlation across services and logs. If absent, gateway must inject one.
2. x-rw-customer-id: string – Customer identifier (for hosted APIs) or empty for internal requests. Must be the canonical id used in billing.
3. x-rw-api-key-hash: sha256 – Non-reversible API key fingerprint used for rate-limiting and quota checks. Never log raw keys.
4. x-rw-traffic-class: one of {interactive, batch, admin, controlplane} – Guides routing, batching, and resource selection.
5. x-rw-priority: integer 0–100 – Optional hint for request prioritization and scheduling.

Suggested trace attributes (OpenTelemetry semantic conventions) to set on the trace/span:
- service.rw.owner = rw.owner value
- service.rw.product = rw.product value
- request.rw.tenant_id = x-rw-customer-id value
- request.rw.traffic_class = x-rw-traffic-class

Propagation and transformation rules:
- Gateways and SDKs must canonicalize header names to lowercase.
- Raw API keys must never be emitted; always replace with a hash before propagation.
- When requests route between deployment boundaries (hosted -> dedicated), preserve the x-rw-request-id to maintain end-to-end traceability.

Enforcement and Validation

Enforcement occurs at three layers: build-time (CI), ingress-time (edge/gateway), and runtime (service sidecar).

- CI checks: New services and infra terraform modules must include metadata tags. A linting step validates presence and allowed values for required tags.
- Ingress validation: Edge and API gateways validate required headers and either reject requests missing mandatory attribution or augment them if the requester is internal. Rejection must return HTTP 400 with a structured error code: RW-ATTR-001.
- Runtime assertions: Service sidecars assert presence of x-rw-request-id and log a WARNING metric if missing. Sidecars augment traces with service.rw.* attributes from tags when available.

Example gateway rejection response (JSON):
{ "error": "missing_attribution", "code": "RW-ATTR-001", "message": "request missing required header: x-rw-customer-id" }

Cost allocation mapping

The billing pipeline maps resource tags and request headers into charge buckets. Rules:

- Customer-billed usage: If x-rw-customer-id is present on a request and the request triggers billable inference tokens, attribute token counts to that customer.
- Shared infrastructure: Resources tagged rw.owner=team-model-serving are billed to that team's internal cost center unless overridden by rw.cost_center.
- SLO-based premium: If rw.slo_class == gold, apply premium rate multiplier to CPU/GPU hourly costs for internal chargeback.

SQL example to roll up usage (simplified):
SELECT
  COALESCE(request.customer_id, resource.tags['rw.owner']) AS billed_entity,
  SUM(tokens) AS total_tokens,
  SUM(cost_usd) AS cost_usd
FROM usage_events
LEFT JOIN resources ON usage_events.resource_id = resources.id
WHERE timestamp >= '{{start}}' AND timestamp < '{{end}}'
GROUP BY billed_entity;

Operational Runbook (adoption and rollout)

1. Inventory: List all services and resources under your team. Export tags and recent request header patterns.
2. Adopt tags: Update IaC modules (Terraform/Helm) to include the required rw.* tags with variables tied to repository metadata.
3. SDK/gateway updates: Ensure SDKs set x-rw-request-id and x-rw-api-key-hash. Gateways must validate and inject missing x-rw-request-id.
4. CI gate: Add tagging linter and header-usage tests to service repositories.
5. Shadow validation: Run ingress validation in shadow mode for 2 weeks (log rejections, do not reject).
6. Enforce: After shadow period and stakeholder signoff, flip to reject mode for missing headers/tags.
7. Audit & iterate: Run weekly audits of tag coverage and header propagation metrics for the first 90 days.

Measurement and SLOs

Key metrics to track (instrumented and exported to central metrics):
- rw.tags.coverage.percent: Percentage of active resources with all required tags (SLO target 99%).
- rw.requests.attributed.percent: Percentage of billable requests carrying x-rw-customer-id (SLO 99.5% for hosted APIs).
- rw.request.id.propagation.latency: Time between gateway request id generation and first span ingest (SLO 200ms).
- rw.attribution.errors: Count of RW-ATTR-001 rejections (SLO target: 0 after enforcement).

Testing and Validation Checklist

- Unit tests for tagging template generation in IaC modules.
- Integration tests where a synthetic request with and without headers is sent through the gateway to a downstream service; assert propagation to traces and logs.
- Load tests to ensure header normalization does not add > 2% CPU overhead on edge tier.
- Cost accounting validation: Reconcile weekly synthetic usage and ensure billed_entity matches expected mapping.

Security and Privacy Considerations

- Never include sensitive customer data or raw API keys in tags or headers. Use hashed identifiers and tenant ids instead.
- Limit access to tag editing via infrastructure RBAC; changes to rw.cost_center or rw.owner must require a permissions review.
- Logs that include request attribution metadata should be redacted for x-rw-api-key-hash where appropriate.

Exceptions and edge cases

- Autonomous background jobs: If a batch job lacks a meaningful x-rw-customer-id, use rw.owner / rw.cost_center for billing. Document exceptions in the service README.
- Third-party integrations: When forwarding requests to external vendors, strip internal-only headers and map attribution to an agreed external attribute.

Appendix: Implementation snippets

Terraform snippet (tags block):
resource "aws_instance" "inference_worker" {
  ami = var.ami
  instance_type = var.instance_type
  tags = merge(var.common_tags, {
    "rw.owner" = var.team_slug,
    "rw.product" = var.product_slug,
    "rw.env" = var.environment,
    "rw.cost_center" = var.cost_center
  })
}

NodeJS middleware example (express):
function attributionMiddleware(req, res, next) {
  if (!req.headers['x-rw-request-id']) {
    req.headers['x-rw-request-id'] = uuidv4();
  }
  // Hash api key if present
  if (req.headers['x-api-key']) {
    req.headers['x-rw-api-key-hash'] = sha256(req.headers['x-api-key']);
    delete req.headers['x-api-key'];
  }
  next();
}

Contact and ownership

- Standards owner: Platform Infra (team infra-platform).
- On-call for enforcement systems: infra-ops (see team wiki for rotation).
- For exceptions and questions: open a ticket in #infra-standards Slack and tag @AshaPatel.
